problem.title: House Robber
problem.statement: There is a row of houses, each containing some money. The rule: you cannot rob two adjacent houses (alarm goes off). Calculate the maximum amount of money you can take.
problem.hint: At each house, you only have two choices: take this house or skip it. If you take it, the previous house must be skipped. If you skip, take the best from before. Try computing two values at each step.
problem.walkthrough:
Example money in houses: [2, 7, 9, 3, 1].

House 1 (2): take=2, skip=0
House 2 (7): take=0+7=7, skip=max(2,0)=2
House 3 (9): take=2+9=11, skip=max(7,2)=7
House 4 (3): take=7+3=10, skip=max(11,7)=11
House 5 (1): take=11+1=12, skip=max(10,11)=11

Answer: max(12, 11) = 12. (Take houses 1 + 3 + 5 = 2+9+1 = 12)

Key insight: at each house, compute two values: if you take this house and if you skip. Moving to the next house, these two values update.
